mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates remain stable.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during an actual NBER-defined recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth offsetting labor weakness.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based contraction in economic activity, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a supply-chain normalization period.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% for two months indicates a dual shock of higher rates and inflation, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% AND CPIAUCSL > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails when real growth remains robust.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) for two consecutive months signals a broad-based collapse in residential demand and consumer spending, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a period of strong export growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above trend by more than 1.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which raises wage pressures and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent, broad-based decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) for six consecutive months, regardless of monetary policy stance, signals deepening economic stagnation and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a synchronized global demand shock.
